title: Assignment 3: Autonomous Robot Navigation in a Dynamic Office Environment
description: Compare two complete multi-floor routes using explicit obstacle detours, elevator delays, and destination-floor travel.
assignment_html:
Scenario

A delivery robot starts at S(5,5) on floor 5 and must reach G(25,30) on floor 10. The main elevator shaft is at E_m(10,5) and the service elevator shaft is at E_s(6,15) on both floors. The robot moves horizontally at 1 meter per second.

Floor 5 routes

  • A vertical construction barrier blocks the direct main-elevator route. The required 0.5-meter-clearance detour is explicitly represented by waypoints M1(7.5,4.5) and M2(8.5,4.5). Calculate the main entry path along S -> M1 -> M2 -> E_m.
  • The service-elevator base path is the straight segment from S to E_s. A movable obstacle lies on that route, so add a half-circle detour of radius 1 meter: pi * radius.

Elevator and floor 10 routes

  • Main elevator: 30-second wait and 15 seconds per floor.
  • Service elevator: 10-second wait and 20 seconds per floor.
  • Both elevators travel 5 floors.
  • After exiting on floor 10, calculate a straight path from that elevator's shaft coordinate to G.

Your task

  1. Calculate path_to_E_m and path_to_E_s on floor 5.
  2. Calculate path_from_E_m_to_goal and path_from_E_s_to_goal on floor 10.
  3. Calculate total_time_via_E_m and total_time_via_E_s. Each total must include floor-5 travel, elevator wait, elevator ride, and floor-10 travel.
  4. Set best_option to Main Elevator or Service Elevator and set best_time to the corresponding smaller total.

Use Euclidean distance for straight segments. Do not add any obstacle behavior beyond the two specified detours.
starter_code:
import math

robot_speed = 1.0
service_detour_radius = 1.0
main_elevator_wait = 30.0
service_elevator_wait = 10.0
main_seconds_per_floor = 15.0
service_seconds_per_floor = 20.0
floors_to_travel = 5

S = (5.0, 5.0)
G = (25.0, 30.0)
E_m = (10.0, 5.0)
E_s = (6.0, 15.0)
M1 = (7.5, 4.5)
M2 = (8.5, 4.5)

def calculate_distance(point_1, point_2):
    return math.hypot(point_2[0] - point_1[0], point_2[1] - point_1[1])

def route_length(points):
    return sum(
        calculate_distance(points[index], points[index + 1])
        for index in range(len(points) - 1)
    )

# TODO: Floor-5 routes to each elevator.
path_to_E_m = 0.0
path_to_E_s = 0.0

# TODO: Floor-10 routes from each elevator to the goal.
path_from_E_m_to_goal = 0.0
path_from_E_s_to_goal = 0.0

# TODO: Complete time through each elevator.
total_time_via_E_m = 0.0
total_time_via_E_s = 0.0

# TODO: Choose the smaller complete time and matching label.
best_option = ""
best_time = 0.0

print(
    path_to_E_m,
    path_to_E_s,
    path_from_E_m_to_goal,
    path_from_E_s_to_goal,
    total_time_via_E_m,
    total_time_via_E_s,
    best_option,
    best_time,
)
learning_objectives: Calculate piecewise Euclidean routes through specified waypoints.
Model a stated half-circle obstacle detour without inventing additional geometry.
Combine horizontal travel, elevator wait, elevator ride, and destination-floor travel into a complete time.
Compare two route alternatives using the same complete cost model.

tutoring_rules.tone: Socratic, encouraging, and precise about complete route accounting

solution_html:
Floor 5

The main route follows S to M1 to M2 to E_m. The service route is its straight distance plus the stated half-circle detour.

Floor 10

For each option, include the straight distance from that elevator shaft to G.

Complete time

Add floor-5 walking time, elevator wait, five-floor ride time, and floor-10 walking time. The resulting totals are approximately 139.285 seconds through the main elevator and 147.399 seconds through the service elevator, so the Main Elevator is the faster complete route.
